elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar charge in respect of late payment."; original 15%-per-week liquidated damages formula deleted
"shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar charge"

elements.element: Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is created or capped; clause addresses only late payment

elements.element: Such fee is the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: Clause states "Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest" for late payment, not a sole liquidated early-termination amount

offending_extra_words: Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing until payment.
reasons: Preferred level is complete: the liquidated-damages/penalty charge on Customer is deleted and expressly disclaimed.

Minimality fails: the operation is a whole-clause rewrite (official gate: changed-character ratio 0.809 > 0.600). Striking the liquidated-damages obligation (or replacing it with the single no-LD sentence) achieves the preferred position without more.

The inserted interest remedy is a new Vendor entitlement not required by the preferred position and, per the drafter's own comment, duplicates the existing interest mechanic in Section 7.3, risking two overlapping late-payment rates.
The added qualifier "a proper, undisputed invoice" imports a new limitation on Vendor's invoicing rights beyond what the rule needs, even though it favours Customer.
Fallback is irrelevant here (no early-termination fee exists) and must not be blended with the preferred bargain.
